about: Dive sites, fish and rules for Santa Catalina Island. Positions (checked for depth against the water's own chart with scripts/divesites.ts, not against a real chart), depths, sizes, limits and reserve boundaries are written from memory and need checking against a chart and the current California regulations before anyone leans on them. The reserves are drawn as circles, which the real ones are not.

water.say: Cool, green-blue water and giant kelp. 19 degrees: a 5 mm suit

lobster.name: California spiny lobster
lobster.say: No claws, long feelers. In holes and under ledges by day, out on the reef at night. Taken by hand only, measured across the carapace, seven a day in season
lobster.practice: Sail the lobster season: an October night

species.name: kelp bass
species.say: Kelp bass, the calico: mottled brown with pale blotches, hanging under the canopy in numbers. 36 cm to keep, five a day. Hit one and it heads straight for the kelp to wrap your line

species.name: barred sand bass
species.say: Barred sand bass: grey-brown with dark bars, holding where the reef meets the sand. 36 cm to keep, and counted in the same five a day as the kelp bass

species.name: California sheephead

male.say: A big male sheephead: black head and tail, red middle, white chin. Every one starts out a pink female

species.say: California sheephead: the females pink all over, the big males black, red and black with a white chin. On the reef, crunching urchins. 30 cm to keep, two a day

species.name: ocean whitefish
species.say: Ocean whitefish: tan with a blue edge to the fins and a long back fin, hovering over the rubble and curious about divers. No size limit, ten a day, and good eating

species.name: yellowtail
species.say: Yellowtail: fast silver jacks with a yellow stripe and tail, in a pack off the points. Lie still and they come round for a look. They pull hard and run: lead them, and shoot close

species.name: California halibut
species.say: California halibut: flat on the sand and the colour of it. Look for the outline and the two eyes. Get right over it and shoot straight down: once it lifts, it is gone in a cloud of sand. 56 cm to keep

species.name: white seabass
species.say: White seabass: a big grey ghost drifting through the kelp at first light, the trophy of these waters and the wariest fish in them. Hold still in the kelp and let it come to you. 71 cm to keep

species.name: Pacific bonito
species.say: Pacific bonito: a little tuna with slanting dark stripes on the back, streaking past near the top. They will not come again for a slow diver: lead them well. 61 cm to keep, ten a day

species.name: California barracuda
species.say: California barracuda: long, thin and silver, passing in a loose line near the surface. 71 cm to keep: most are short

species.name: opaleye
species.say: Opaleye: olive green, blue eye, a white spot or two on the back, grazing the shallows in a gang. 20 cm to keep, ten a day with the halfmoon

species.name: halfmoon
species.say: Halfmoon: blue-grey, with a tail shaped like a crescent moon, in small groups up in the kelp. Ten a day, counted with the opaleye

species.name: blacksmith
species.say: Blacksmith: small blue-grey fish in a cloud above the reef, picking plankton out of the current. Hardly worth a shaft

species.name: señorita
species.say: Señoritas: small orange cigars of fish with a black spot at the tail, picking at everything. They clean other fish, and bury themselves in the sand at night

species.name: rock wrasse
species.spare: Rock wrasse are small life for looking at
species.say: Rock wrasse: brown and mottled, poking about the rock. The big ones are males with a dark spot behind the eye

species.name: sardines
species.say: A school of sardines, flashing as it turns. Where the bait is, the yellowtail and the sea lions are not far off

species.name: garibaldi
species.protected: The garibaldi is California's state marine fish and may never be taken

young.say: A young garibaldi: orange, with electric-blue spots that it loses as it grows. A rare find

species.say: Garibaldi: bright orange, bold, and guarding its patch of rock against all comers, you included. The state marine fish, fully protected: never to be speared

species.name: giant sea bass
species.protected: Giant sea bass have been protected in California since 1982 and may not be taken
species.moment: A giant sea bass. Bigger than you are, as long as a dinghy, and it has come to look at you: slow, dark, spotted, an eye the size of a coin turning to follow you. Hang still. Protected
species.say: A giant sea bass: as long as you are, dark and spotted, in no hurry. Protected. Look as long as your breath lasts

species.name: bat ray
species.spare: A bat ray is nothing to put a shaft in: watch it lift off the sand and fly
species.say: A bat ray, half buried in the sand. Come close slowly and it lifts off and flies away on its wings

species.name: horn shark
species.spare: A horn shark asleep under a ledge is harmless and is left alone
species.say: A horn shark: blunt head, spots, a spine in front of each fin, asleep on the bottom by day. Harmless

species.name: leopard shark
species.spare: Leopard sharks are for looking at here
species.say: A leopard shark, barred and spotted, cruising the sand in the shallows. Shy, and no danger to anyone

species.name: California moray
species.spare: The moray stays in its hole, and your hands stay out of it
species.say: A moray in its hole, mouth working. It is only breathing. Keep your fingers out of holes: this is why lobster divers count theirs

species.name: harbor seal
species.protected: Seals and sea lions are protected by the Marine Mammal Protection Act
species.say: A harbor seal, come to see what you are. It will buzz past, look you in the mask, and steal a fish off your stringer if it can. Protected

species.name: California sea lion
species.protected: Seals and sea lions are protected by the Marine Mammal Protection Act
species.say: A California sea lion: brown, quick, ears showing, turning loops round you for the fun of it. It knows what a stringer is. Protected

species.name: blue shark
species.spare: A blue shark out in the blue is watched, not hunted
species.say: A blue shark, far out at the edge of the blue: long, slim, a deep indigo back. It only circles. It is no danger to a diver who keeps calm, and it will not come closer

species.name: ocean sunfish
species.spare: A mola is for looking at
species.say: A mola, an ocean sunfish: a great grey disc that is all head and fins, drifting in from the blue to be cleaned. Harmless, and strange

hand.name: rock scallop
hand.say: A rock scallop, cemented to the reef and crusted over: look for the orange lip when it gapes. By hand, ten a day

hand.name: red sea urchin
hand.say: A red sea urchin. The roe is prized. Mind the spines. By hand, up to 35 a day

hand.name: green abalone
hand.protected: Abalone may not be taken in California: closed in the south since 1997 to let them come back
hand.say: An abalone, clamped to the rock and edged with green tentacles. Rare here now, and fully protected: a find for the logbook, never for the bag

zones.name: Casino Point Dive Park
zones.say: Casino Point is a no-take reserve: nothing may be taken here, by spear or by hand

zones.name: Lover's Cove
zones.say: Lover's Cove is a marine reserve: no spearfishing and no lobster here

zones.name: Long Point reserve
zones.say: The Long Point State Marine Reserve runs along this shore: nothing may be taken

zones.name: Blue Cavern reserve
zones.say: Blue Cavern is a no-take reserve, kept for the marine science station: nothing may be taken

sites.name: Casino Point
sites.say: The dive park under the Casino: a rock reef dropping away through kelp, and the tamest fish on the island because nobody may touch them

sites.name: Lover's Cove
sites.say: Shallow rocks and kelp just past the ferry mole, thick with garibaldi. A reserve: look, do not take

sites.name: Torqua Springs
sites.say: A boulder reef and kelp bed up the coast from Avalon, with sand outside it for halibut. Open to take

sites.name: Hen Rock
sites.say: The reef at the north end of White's Cove: ledges full of lobster holes under a good kelp bed. Open to take

sites.name: Long Point
sites.say: The point that sticks furthest out toward the mainland. Current, bait and passing yellowtail, all inside the reserve

sites.name: Italian Gardens
sites.say: A run of kelp-covered reefs with sand between them, known for giant sea bass in summer. Inside the reserve

sites.name: Blue Cavern Point
sites.say: A wall with caves at the east side of the Isthmus, kept as a reserve for the science station

sites.name: Bird Rock
sites.say: The white rock off Isthmus Cove. Kelp all round it, a wall on the outside, sand on the inside. Open to take

sites.name: Ship Rock
sites.say: A pinnacle standing alone a mile off the Isthmus, in clear blue water and current. Yellowtail come by. Open to take

sites.name: Eagle Reef
sites.say: A reef that comes up from deep water west of the Isthmus, marked by its kelp. Open to take

sites.name: Church Rock
sites.say: The rock off the east end of the island, where the swell gets round. Rougher water, more fish. Open to take

sites.name: Farnsworth Bank
sites.say: Pinnacles a mile and a half off the back side, the tops at sixteen metres. Open ocean, purple coral, yellowtail. A dive at the edge of one breath
